ideas.idea: Rung 186: read the underspecified layered cap convolution (2.15) of OpenAI's companion as a split of the retained configuration by the layer of its largest fragment over ALL cap values occurring in the outer and face domains, with the erased coordinate admitted in the outer shells whose cap is >= the layer value.
ideas.note: Session 14: with this reading our J_lambda,H lands 5.9e-9 above the published lower bound and the ratio matches (code/oai186_J.py); a fresh-context audit found no defect.

ideas.idea: Exploration: could the slack in Song-Yue's exponent conditions raise the level enough to move the variational criterion from k = 48 to k = 47?
ideas.note: Session 14: k = 47 needs d omega >= 5.8e-4; the loosest printed margin (Type III (52)) allows 1.4e-4, IIa (33) 2.2e-5 (code/explore/level_slack.py; heuristic).

ideas.idea: Probabilistic model check: prime pairs in translates of the Lean-checked 236-tuple vs the Hardy-Littlewood prediction, and whether data can say anything about DHL[48,2].
ideas.note: Session 13: HL fits to 3e-4 at X = 1e8 (known); the mean number of primes per translate is 48/log X > 1 until X ~ 7e20, so no computable range bears on DHL[48,2]. notes/explorations.md.

ideas.idea: Split Corr2 into its Q(u',R)^2 and Q(u',U)^2 parts (both >= 0) and apply the Bonferroni truncation to each (upper bound with j <= 2 for the first, lower bound with j <= 1 for the second), so that one-sided certificates need no j = 3 pieces at all.
ideas.note: Session 14: paper Prop. prop:bonf2 and capped_exact.py --bonf. On the 240 vector: 4.012038868083 > 4 from 98 pieces (no j = 3 piece), 3.5e-8 below exact; the R and U parts are each ~35x their difference but their levels decay fast.

ideas.idea: Skip the thin inclusion-exclusion pieces (j = 3 extra coordinates above g) with a rigorous a priori bound (volume of the thin region times a sup bound for the integrand) when only the sign of the criterion is needed, not exact equality.
ideas.note: Session 13: Bonferroni (paper Prop. prop:bonf, Proved here): for a one-sided certificate the Corr1 pieces with j = 3 and the I-correction pieces with j >= 2 can be dropped (their integrands are >= 0), no bound needed; on the Song-Yue witness the dropped Corr1 level is -2.5e-69 J and cost 7.1 of 32.2 core-hours. The crude a priori bound (code/thin_bound.py: coefficient-sum sup times region volume) gives 1.4e-14 J for Corr1 j = 3 but 6e32 J for Corr2 j = 3, so it does not settle Corr2 (unsigned integrand).

ideas.idea: Toy capped problem at k = 3 with per-m caps (caps on single coordinates and on pair sums): does the cap pattern explain the 31% regain at k = 45?
ideas.note: Session 12: pair caps give a SMALLER regain (0.04-0.085) than single caps (<= 0.13); mixing never exceeds ~13%. The cap pattern alone does not explain k = 45 (notes/explorations.md).

ideas.idea: Integrate products of monomial symmetric functions over the simplex by summing over partial matchings of their parts (bitmask DP), so a witness given in the monomial basis can be checked without converting to power sums.
ideas.note: Session 10: songyue_I0.py / songyue_J0.py reproduce Song-Yue's Iref exactly in 25 s and the cap-free J0 in 33 s; an independent check of the power-sum route.

ideas.idea: Read the step of [Sta26, Lemma 5] that Song-Yue (Remark 4.23) say lacks a hypothesis.
ideas.note: Session 10: confirmed against arXiv v1 that the gamma in (1/2, 1/2+2omega+eps] step applies Lemma 3 with alpha as the short factor without a Siegel-Walfisz hypothesis on alpha; whether the alphas that occur satisfy it (a repair) is not checked.

ideas.idea: Dilation identity M_k(L,tau) = 4 A1 M_{k, eps/A1} plus the two-zone dual weight, to bound the one-band hybrid supports of 2026 as a function of the level omega.
ideas.note: Theorem 25: no k ≤ 28 at Stadlmann's omega = 0.003, no k ≤ 26 at omega = 0.007, no k ≤ 22 for omega ≤ 1/68, for any delta, caps and minorant. The same weight fails at the next k.

ideas.idea: Rigorous capped ratio from a polynomial P: penalise the exact integral of P^2 over the cap-violation set in a generalised eigenproblem, bound J_T by Cauchy-Schwarz.
ideas.note: Superseded in session 6: the Cauchy-Schwarz treatment of J_T, not the caps, caused the loss (3.9597); exact J_T gives 4.0120.

ideas.idea: Union bound for the cap-violation set over m-subsets with sum above the cap, dropping the condition that each coordinate exceeds delta.
ideas.note: Hopelessly loose: E/I ≈ 146 for the cap-free optimiser at degree 20 (the m = 4..6 terms explode).

ideas.idea: Optimise Lemma 13 over ALL weights psi_m = Psi(S - t_m, t_m) (the family containing Cor. 6.4 and the two-zone weight) as a convex program, to learn the limit of this family.
ideas.note: Discretised optimum ≈ 4.14 at (k, eps) = (50, 1/25) vs truth ≥ 4.0012; equals k/(k-1) log k at eps = 0. The family cannot reach the true threshold; need weights seeing more of t (Proposition 19).

ideas.note: Theorem 15: no k ≤ 29 for any eps < 1, beating the k ≤ 23 floor from Polymath8b Prop. 6.5.

ideas.idea: Exponential-moment generating function for simplex integrals of power-sum products, to make certified high-degree computations cheap.
ideas.note: Lemma 3. Builds a 471x471 exact Gram pair in about 15 s.

ideas.idea: Use the exact capped evaluator to test which of Charton et al.'s two cap sets (Table 3 vs Lemma 9.1) supports their k = 45 criterion.
ideas.note: Table 3 caps: 4.0027 > 4 (two programs). Lemma 9.1 caps: no P in our 846-dim space reaches 4 (certified ceiling, session 8), so the draft's 4.00438 must use Table 3's caps.

ideas.idea: Reverse-mode (adjoint) differentiation of the exact capped evaluator to get the Gram matrices of I_T and J_T at the cost of one evaluation, then optimise P on the capped support and certify ceilings for a whole test space.
ideas.note: Exact self-tests at k = 12, 49, 45 plus an exact Schwartz-Zippel test at a random vector (k = 45); k = 49 optimum 4.0124198 (two exact programs); Lemma 9.1 ceiling 3.99 certified.

ideas.idea: Heuristic: re-optimising on the capped support regains only a small fraction (about 10%) of what truncation costs, because the truncation acts as a perturbation and the Rayleigh quotient gains only to second order.
ideas.note: Registered prediction 3.977-3.981 for the Lemma 9.1 caps; the optimum is 3.98555. Re-optimising regains 9% of the truncation loss at k = 49 but 31% at k = 45, so a fixed fraction is wrong, and a pure second-order (loss^2/gap) rule is wrong too.

ideas.idea: Schwartz-Zippel check of the reverse pass: compare the quadratic forms from the Gram weights with an exact forward evaluator at one random integer vector, instead of trusting a few structured self-tests.
ideas.note: Exact agreement at k = 45 (Lemma 9.1 caps) with capped_check.py: the two degree-2 forms agree with failure probability < 2^-31 each.

papers.title: An independent exact verification of the variational step behind the claimed 2026 bounds H1 <= 240 and H1 <= 236, with a remark on the caps of a 212 draft
papers.summary: Exact recomputation of the variational criteria of Stadlmann (240), Kintali / Song-Yue (236; two programs) and Charton et al. (212, Table 3 caps); ceiling < 3.99 for the Lemma 9.1 caps; one-sided Bonferroni certificates; the main terms of the 186 companion recomputed. Analytic inputs not verified.
